descriptive-statistics.def: Numbers that summarize a set of data, such as the mean, median, mode, range and standard deviation.

frequency-distribution.def: A table or graph showing how often each value, or each range of values, occurs in a set of data. A histogram shows it as touching bars.

central-tendency.def: A single value that describes the center of a set of data: the mean, the median or the mode.

mean.def: The arithmetic average: the sum of the values divided by how many values there are, written $\bar{x}$.

median.def: The middle value when the data are put in order; with an even number of values, halfway between the two middle ones.

mode-stat.def: The value that occurs most often in a set of data.

bimodal.def: A distribution with two peaks, or two modes, often because two different groups are mixed together.

variation.def: How spread out the values in a set of data are; measured by the range and the standard deviation.

range-stat.def: The highest value minus the lowest value in a set of data.

standard-deviation.def: A measure of variation: roughly the typical distance of the values from the mean. A larger standard deviation means more spread.

outlier.def: A value far from the rest of the data. An outlier pulls the mean toward it but barely moves the median.

skew.def: A lopsided distribution with a long tail on one side: positively skewed when the tail stretches toward high values, negatively skewed when it stretches toward low values. The mean is pulled toward the tail.
